keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). Khosrow II page: Vistahm 'soon held sway in the entire eastern and northern quadrants of the Iranian realm', 'from the Oxus River to Ardabil', and also subdued two Hephthalite princes of Transoxiana (not drawn). The Vistahm page says he 'began to threaten Media' and retreated to Gilan; Media is not drawn. Neither page gives an area or a boundary, so Khorasan, Tabaristan and a 120 km disc round Ardabil are the researcher's reading. The Vistahm page lists no capital.

region.text: Tabaristan and west to the region of Ardabil: the north of Vistahm's domain 'from the Oxus River to Ardabil'; Khorasan comes in the gain of August 591, when Bahram Chobin is beaten

ledger.note: c. 590/1: Vistahm, Khosrow II's uncle and spahbed of the East, claims the throne and holds the north and east of Iran. Vistahm page: 'The commonly accepted dates are ca. 590-596'; the infobox gives 'King of Kings of Iran and non-Iran' 590/1-596 or 594/5-600; Howard-Johnston and Pourshariati push the outbreak to 594/5. He announced his claim by letter, citing descent from Darius III. The year is the infobox's first year, 591. fx-29 (F138): found region cut to Tabaristan and Ardabil, because Iranian Khorasan was Bahram Chobin's until he was beaten at Blarathon (August 591) and the compiler gave the 895 shared cells to Bahram for the whole year and then, at Bahram's death, to the Sasanian Empire; Khorasan now arrives by the gain below.

region.text: the East: Khorasan, which Bahram Chobin held as governor and ruler until Blarathon and which Khosrow II then put under Vistahm

ledger.note: August 591: Khorasan passes from the beaten Bahram to Vistahm. Vistahm page: after Blarathon 'Khosrow rewarded his uncles with high positions' and 'Vistahm received the post of spahbed of the East, encompassing Tabaristan and Khorasan'; the Blarathon page dates the battle 'August 591' and has Bahram and 4,000 men escape 'east to Nishapur'. The page does not say Vistahm took the land from Bahram, nor the month of the grant; August 591 is the battle's month. Mirror of bahram-chobin /ledger/2. Bahram Chobin page: he 'was given the governorship of Khorasan' in 588.

ledger.note: c. 596: Vistahm is murdered during the battle near Qumis and the rebellion is finished. Vistahm page: he 'was murdered by Pariowk at Khosrow's urging' near Qumis (an alternative account credits his wife Gordiya); 'it required another expedition by Smbat in the next year to finally end the rebellion'. The page gives no year for his death; the infobox says 596 or 600 and the coinage shows a rebellion of seven years.

wars.outcome: After several failed armies Khosrow II called on the Armenian Smbat Bagratuni, whose army engaged Vistahm near Qumis; Vistahm was murdered in the battle and Smbat's second expedition the next year ended the rebellion.
wars.note: The year range is the infobox 590/1-596 plus the following year's expedition; the Vistahm page gives no year for the first engagement. Khosrow II page: Vistahm's forces 'repelled the royal army' at Qumis. [Reviewer me-06-x, 2026-10-19: war end set to 596, the dossier's end year; the page's 'another expedition by Smbat in the next year' that ended the rebellion is undated]

certainty.note: A rebel realm described only as 'the eastern and northern quadrants of the Iranian realm'; no frontier on either page.

Rebel state Cliopatria lacks (new_slug vistahm; type rebel, rule 5). Pages opened: Vistahm, Khosrow II. The Sasanian civil war of 589-591 page does not mention Vistahm's own rebellion (it has him with Vinduyih overthrowing Hormizd IV and raising an army in Azerbaijan for Khosrow), so the 589-591 war is in the bahram-chobin dossier, not here.

COUNTERPART EVENTS MISSING: the sasanian-empire dossier has no loss to vistahm (591) or gain back (596); the Sasanian gap-filler should add them. No capital: the Vistahm page names none (empty capitals list). The Hephthalite princes Shaug and Pariowk of Transoxiana are subdued vassals, not drawn.

UNSETTLED: dates (590/1-596 or 594/5-600; no year for the death or for the Qumis battle; if the second expedition fell the year after 596 the rebellion ended in 597); the western limit ('region of Ardabil') and whether Media and Gilan were held. Gazetteer: all names resolve.
